result.topic_en: Euler discusses conditions under which a number N can be resolved into three triangular numbers, based on the roots of three-triangular decompositions of smaller numbers N−p, and tabulates such decompositions for numbers 1–12, then examines N=13.
result.transcription:
192 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
Inde pro $p$ sequentes oriuntur valores $d=-2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,\ 5$
$n=1$: $p=$ $0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,\ 5,\ 6$
$n=2$: $p=$ $2,\ 4,\ 6,\ 8,\ 10,\ 12,\ 14$
$n=3$: $p=$ $3,\ 6,\ 9,\ 12,\ 15,\ 18,\ 21,\ 24$
$n=4$: $p=$ $8,\ 12,\ 16,\ 20,\ 24,\ 28,\ 32,\ 36$
etc. etc.
Unde pro diversis valoribus ipsius $p$ resolutio numeri $N$ in tres trigonales succedet, si fuerit pro numeris minoribus
tum erit et
$N-1$: $b=a$ $x=a-1$ $y=b+1$
$N-2$ $\begin{cases} b=a+1 \\ b=a-1 \end{cases}$ $\begin{matrix} x=a-1 \\ x=a-2 \end{matrix}$ $\begin{matrix} y=b+1 \\ y=b+2 \end{matrix}$
$N-3$ $\begin{cases} b=a+2 \\ b=a-2 \end{cases}$ $\begin{matrix} x=a-1 \\ x=a-3 \end{matrix}$ $\begin{matrix} y=b+1 \\ y=b+3 \end{matrix}$
$N-4$ $\begin{cases} b=a+3 \\ b=a \\ b=a-3 \end{cases}$ $\begin{matrix} x=a-1 \\ x=a-2 \\ x=a-4 \end{matrix}$ $\begin{matrix} y=b+1 \\ y=b+2 \\ y=b+4 \end{matrix}$
His positis ambarum $x$ et $y$ inventio succedet, si inter ternas radices $a,\ b,\ c$, primo pro numero $N-1$ fuerit
$b=a$, sive si duae fuerint aequales. Secundo si pro numero $N-2$ fuerit vel $b=a+1$, vel $b=a-1$, hoc
est si differentia fuerit inter binas $=1$, tum vero duplex solutio locum habebit. Tertio si pro $N-3$ fuerit
vel $b=a+2$, vel $b=a-2$, hoc est si binae radices binario discrepent. Quarto si pro numero $N-4$ fuerit vel
$b=a+3$, vel $b=a$, vel $b=a-3$, hoc est si differentia inter binas radices fuerint vel $=0$, vel $=3$. Quinto si pro
numero $N-5$ fuerit $b=a\pm4$ h. e. si differentia inter binas radices fuerit $=\pm4$. Sexto si pro numero $N-6$
fuerit vel $b=a\pm5$, vel $b=a\pm1$, hoc est si inter radices binas occurrat differentia vel 1, vel 5. Quamobrem
si demonstrari posset, semper unum saltem horum casuum locum habere debere, tum demonstratum foret,
omnes numeros esse summas trium trigonalium. Quod cum de minoribus numeris certum per se sit, pro ma-
joribus autem continuo plures casus examinandi occurrant, eo minus dubitari potest, quin resolutio semper sit
locum habitura, idque plerumque pluribus modis, quo accedit, quod pro majoribus numeris fere omnes numeri
$N-p$ pluribus modis in tres trigonales resolvi possint. Quod quo clarius pateat has resolutiones ab ipso initio
numerorum secundum ternas radices contemplemur:
numeri | radices $a,\ b,\ c$ | vel radices | vel radices
1 | 0, 0, 1 | |
2 | 0, 1, 1 | |
3 | 1, 1, 1 | 0, 0, 2 |
4 | 0, 1, 2 | |
5 | 1, 1, 2 | |
6 | 0, 2, 2 | 0, 0, 3 |
7 | 1, 2, 2 | 0, 1, 3 |
8 | 1, 1, 3 | |
9 | 2, 2, 2 | 0, 2, 3 |
10 | 0, 0, 4 | 1, 2, 3 |
11 | 0, 1, 4 | |
12 | 0, 3, 3 | 1, 1, 4 | 2, 2, 3
Hinc ergo examinemus numerum $N=13$ et habebimus
$a,\ b,\ c$
pro $N-1=12$: 0, 3, 3
1, 1, 4
2, 2, 3
pro $N-2=11$: 0, 1, 4
pro $N-3=10$: 0, 0, 4
1, 2, 3
pro $N-4=9$: 2, 2, 2
0, 2, 3
pro $N-5=8$: 1, 1, 3
etc. etc.

methods.what: Table of values of p (as function of n and d) to be subtracted from N in reducing a three-triangular representation of N to one of N−p
Rules deriving a three-triangular resolution of N from a resolution of N−p with roots a, b depending on the difference b−a (new roots x, y)
Criterion: N is a sum of three triangular numbers if N−p has a representation whose two roots differ by a specified amount (0, 1, 2, 0 or 3, ±4, 1 or 5 for p=1..6)
methods.quote:
si inter ternas radices $a,\ b,\ c$, primo pro numero $N-1$ fuerit
$b=a$, sive si duae fuerint aequales

methods.what: Table of representations of numbers 1–12 as sums of three triangular numbers by their roots
Worked example applying the criterion to N=13
methods.quote: Hinc ergo examinemus numerum $N=13$ et habebimus

items.quote:
Quamobrem
si demonstrari posset, semper unum saltem horum casuum locum habere debere, tum demonstratum foret,
omnes numeros esse summas trium trigonalium.
items.english: Therefore, if it could be proved that at least one of these cases must always occur, then it would be proved that all numbers are sums of three triangular numbers.

items.quote:
eo minus dubitari potest, quin resolutio semper sit
locum habitura, idque plerumque pluribus modis
items.english: so much the less can it be doubted that the resolution will always take place, and usually in several ways

items.quote:
pro majoribus numeris fere omnes numeri
$N-p$ pluribus modis in tres trigonales resolvi possint
items.english: for larger numbers almost all the numbers N−p can be resolved into three triangular numbers in several ways

items.quote:
Quod quo clarius pateat has resolutiones ab ipso initio
numerorum secundum ternas radices contemplemur
items.english: To make this clearer, let us consider these resolutions from the very beginning of the numbers according to their three roots
